label: River
_model: Wild kernel in moving water. The appetite belongs to the river — it wants to be asked before it is crossed, to carry things away, to run where it has always run, and to be given somebody rather than have to take them. Claimants are the river's own names.

appetites.want: that nothing should get over it without asking
appetites.purpose: every crossing would be by its leave

appeasement.move: ask the water leave before you set foot in it

appetites.want: that everything given to it should be carried away for good
appetites.purpose: nothing would ever come back upstream
appetites.asks: "Are you going to let go of that?"

appeasement.move: put something into the water and let it go

appetites.want: that it should run exactly where it has always run
appetites.purpose: the old channel would still be the channel

appeasement.move: walk a stretch of the old course, end to end

appetites.want: to be given somebody, rather than to have to take them
appetites.purpose: nobody would ever have to be taken

appeasement.move: give the water something you could not afford to lose

pole.label: the pole the ferry was worked with
pole.function: the only thing that ever got anybody over and back

float.label: the one thing the river ever brought back upstream
float.function: the only thing it gave up after it had it

mark.label: the mark cut where the old channel ran
mark.function: the only record of where the water actually belongs

gift.label: what was given willingly, the one year
gift.function: the only time it did not have to take anybody

factions.name: the Given
factions.essence: went in willingly, once a year, and are still down there being polite about it

factions.name: the bargees
factions.essence: were working the reach when the water changed and cannot get off it

factions.name: what lives in the deep pool
factions.essence: was here before the river had a name

factions.name: what the river left behind
factions.essence: is still in the old course, waiting for the water to come back

triggerGlossary.announced: came down to the water in the open and stood at the edge
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: seen from the water twice, on both banks
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice over water, which carries the length of a reach
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed on the bank long enough for the water to work at it
triggerGlossary.disturbed: set foot in the ford, moved a mark, or took something off the water

skirmish.line: 3 Giant Rats in the withy beds

foes.name: Giant Rat
foes.note: swim as fast as you wade

skirmish.avoid: get onto dry ground and they will not follow up the bank

fight.line: 3 Ghouls of the drowned on the bank

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit; they fight better in water

fight.avoid: they will not leave the waterline — ten paces up the bank and they stop

battle.line: 1 Troll under the bridge and 2 Ghouls in the shallows

foes.name: Troll
foes.note: REGENERATES 2 Grit a round unless the wound was burnt; wet, so fire is hard here

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

battle.harmedBy: anything, but the Troll only stays down if fire touches it, and everything here is wet — say so before initiative
battle.avoid: it holds the bridge and takes a toll; pay it and it lets you over

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith at the ford, 1 Troll and 4 Ghouls

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest, fire for the Troll and it is wet
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

crossing.dangerLine: the river is crossable in four places and it is paying attention to all of them

institution: a ford, a ferry, a bridge and a weir, and forty miles of nothing between them
a crossing that is safe at one state of water and at no other
banks cut down on both sides where everybody goes in
ritual: leave asked at the water's edge before anybody steps in
the ferry worked across and back empty, each time
a coin put on the parapet by everyone who uses the bridge
demand: a ford with the water at exactly the height it is safe at
a ferry lying at the far bank with the rope slack
a parapet with a row of coins and one gap
wound: a ford with the bottom washed out and the marker poles still standing
a ferry rope cut on the far side
a bridge with the parapet gone and the coins in the water
anchor: the pole the ferry was worked with
a set of marker poles that still read true
a bridge that has never been taken by the water

features: marker poles standing in the ford
a ferry lying at the far bank
a row of coins with one gap
a cut rope end at a landing
a bottom washed out under the poles
a parapet down into the water

decisions.cue: a ford with the water at exactly the height it is safe at
decisions.cost: the height is right and the bottom may not be

resolve.success: you read the bottom off the marker poles and cross dry-shod, all of you
resolve.failure: you go in on the height alone and the bottom is gone under you: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: go round to the bridge, costing a Turn and a toll

decisions.cue: a ferry lying at the far bank with the rope gone slack
decisions.cost: hauling it over takes both banks and there is only one of you on this side

resolve.success: you get the ferry across and have a crossing you control for the whole delve
resolve.failure: you haul on a rope that is cut and go in with it
resolve.orElse: swim it; you cross wet, cold and without your gear, and the water notes it

decisions.cue: a parapet with a row of coins along it and one gap
decisions.cost: the coin is a toll and the gap is somebody who did not pay

resolve.success: you fill the gap and the bridge is yours to cross, both ways, unbothered
resolve.failure: you take a coin instead and the bridge takes the equivalent: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: cross without paying; something under the bridge follows you the whole reach

decisions.cue: marker poles standing in a ford with the bottom washed out under them
decisions.cost: the poles say safe and the river disagrees

resolve.success: you reset the poles honestly and the crossing works for whoever comes after
resolve.failure: you leave them and somebody uses them later, and that is on you
resolve.orElse: pull the poles down; nothing crosses here again, including you

decisions.cue: a ferry rope cut clean on the far side
decisions.cost: somebody cut it from the bank you are not on

resolve.success: you work out who cut it and why, and it is the whole shape of the transgression
resolve.failure: you splice and cross, and it is cut again while you are mid-stream
resolve.orElse: leave it; the far bank is reachable only by the deep pool

decisions.cue: a bridge with the parapet gone and coins visible in the water beneath
decisions.cost: somebody swept the tolls off into the river

resolve.success: you retrieve enough to pay the arrears and the bridge lets everything over
resolve.failure: you take them for yourself and every crossing after costs you double
resolve.orElse: leave them; the toll is outstanding and the bridge collects it another way

situations.doing: working an empty ferry across and back with a pole
situations.onArrival: he brings it in to your bank and waits without speaking
situations.because: the ferry is worked across and back and nobody has been aboard
situations.offer: get aboard and he will take you across anything, once

situations.doing: standing waist-deep at the ford, facing the far bank
situations.onArrival: it turns its head and asks whether you are going over
situations.because: it was taken at the ford and never got over
situations.offer: cross beside it and the water lets you both over

situations.doing: waiting at a landing with a boat and nowhere to take it
situations.onArrival: they ask whether the weir is passable yet
situations.because: the reach closed at both ends with them on it
situations.offer: tell them and they will carry you the whole length of the water

situations.doing: lying along a parapet with one gap in the line
situations.onArrival: the coins are bright and the stone under them is not
situations.because: everybody pays and one did not
situations.offer: put a coin in the gap and the bridge will not let anything follow you

situations.doing: running at exactly the height it is safe at, and no other
situations.onArrival: the water is glass-flat and there is a wind on the trees
situations.because: it is crossable here and it likes to be asked first
situations.offer: ask leave aloud and it will be crossable whenever you come back

situations.doing: standing in the shallows in the shape of a woman up to the knee
situations.onArrival: the water around her does not move at all
situations.because: she takes one at every crossing and has not been given one
situations.offer: offer her something instead and she will let the whole party over

temptations.benefit: once, cross anything on foot
temptations.standingDrawback: the ferry cannot be worked while you have it

temptations.cue: a toll coin off the parapet
temptations.benefit: once, pass a thing that takes tolls
temptations.standingDrawback: the toll is now outstanding in your name

temptations.cue: a set of true marker poles
temptations.benefit: read any crossing correctly
temptations.standingDrawback: the crossing you left unmarked catches somebody

temptations.benefit: once, get everybody across together
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever is on the far bank comes over on it too

temptations.benefit: once, enter water safely
temptations.standingDrawback: leave is given for one crossing, and it counts them

current.dangerLine: the river takes things away and it has been taking them away from here for a long time

institution: a reach that runs one way and has never once run the other
eddies at every bend where everything it carries collects
a mill race that takes whatever the river is carrying and stops it
ritual: something floated off at the head of the reach every year
the eddies raked out each spring and what is in them laid on the bank
a float sent down to see whether the reach is clear
demand: an eddy turning slowly with something in it that has not come out
a float sent down and not arrived
a mill race with the hatch up and nothing coming through
wound: an eddy raked out and everything in it left on the bank, named
a reach with the current running backwards for a hundred yards
a race choked with what it stopped
anchor: the one thing the river ever brought back upstream
an eddy that gives up what it holds

features: an eddy turning with something in it
a float that has not arrived
a race hatch up and nothing coming
things laid out on a bank, named
current running the wrong way
a mill race choked

decisions.cue: an eddy turning slowly with something in it that has not come out
decisions.cost: reaching in gets it and puts you in the turn

resolve.success: you get it out clean and it is what somebody at the ending needs to see
resolve.failure: you go in after it and the eddy has you for a round: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it turning; it turns behind you the whole delve, and you know what is in it

decisions.cue: a float sent down the reach that has not arrived
decisions.cost: something between here and there stopped it

resolve.success: you work out where it stopped and what is there, before you get to it
resolve.failure: you send another and follow it, and arrive where the first one did
resolve.orElse: send nothing; you walk the reach blind, and it is not clear

decisions.cue: a mill race with the hatch up and nothing at all coming through
decisions.cost: the race is stopped and the river is not

resolve.success: you clear the race and what it has been stopping comes through, and it is a lot
resolve.failure: you open it wider and it comes through all at once, onto you
resolve.orElse: leave the hatch; the water is going somewhere else and that is where the ending is

decisions.cue: things raked out of the eddies and laid on the bank, each with a name
decisions.cost: somebody has been recovering and naming them for years

resolve.success: you find who has been doing it and they know every name the river has taken
resolve.failure: you disturb the row and the names come off, and cannot be put back
resolve.orElse: walk past; you have no names for anything at the ending

decisions.cue: a reach with the current running backwards for a hundred yards
decisions.cost: the river is doing something it does not do

resolve.success: you find what is making it run back and can use it to go up the reach
resolve.failure: you go into it and are carried the wrong way, fast, into the pool
resolve.orElse: stay on the bank; the reach is walked, slowly, and the water watches

decisions.cue: a thing lying on the shingle that the river brought back up
decisions.cost: the river gave something back, once, and that is the leverage

resolve.success: you take it and understand what makes it give things up, and can ask again
resolve.failure: you take it as salvage and the river takes the equivalent off you
resolve.orElse: leave it; nothing here is negotiable and the ending is fought

situations.doing: turning slowly at a bend with something pale in it
situations.onArrival: the turn slows while you watch and then resumes
situations.because: everything the river carries collects here and one thing will not go on
situations.offer: take what is in it and the river will carry you rather than take you

situations.doing: laying things out along the bank in a row and naming each one
situations.onArrival: he asks whether you have lost anybody
situations.because: he has been recovering and naming since before the reach closed
situations.offer: give him a name and he will give you what the water took with it

situations.doing: standing chest-deep in the current facing upstream
situations.onArrival: it does not move at all and the water goes round it
situations.because: it went in willingly and the river never carried it off
situations.offer: ask it to move and it will, and the reach clears the whole way down

situations.doing: standing with the hatch up and nothing coming through it
situations.onArrival: the water above the hatch is higher than it should be
situations.because: the race stops what the river carries and it is full
situations.offer: clear it and everything the river has been holding comes down at once, usefully

situations.doing: running backwards along a hundred yards of the reach
situations.onArrival: sticks on the surface go up past you at walking pace
situations.because: the river is doing something it does not do
situations.offer: go up with it and it will put you where nothing else could

situations.doing: lying full length in the shallows in the shape of a drowned man
situations.onArrival: the water around him runs uphill an inch
situations.because: he carries things away and he has stopped
situations.offer: give him something to carry and the reach runs true again

temptations.cue: the thing the river brought back
temptations.benefit: once, get back something the water took
temptations.standingDrawback: the river takes something of equal weight, and chooses

temptations.benefit: once, recover what an eddy holds
temptations.standingDrawback: the eddy takes you in to the waist each time

temptations.cue: a name off the row on the bank
temptations.benefit: once, be known to the drowned
temptations.standingDrawback: they take you for that person

temptations.benefit: once, stop what the water is carrying
temptations.standingDrawback: it stacks up behind, and then comes at once

temptations.benefit: once, know what is ahead of you on the water
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever is ahead sees it coming too

course.dangerLine: the river was moved and it has never accepted that it was

institution: an old channel running dry beside a new one running full
embankments raised on both sides for eight miles
a straight cut where every other stretch of the water wanders
ritual: the banks walked each spring and the marks checked
the old course kept clear of building, by custom, though it is dry
a stone cut where the water used to run
demand: a dry channel with water standing in the bottom of it after no rain
an embankment with a wet patch on the dry side
a mark cut for the old course, still legible
wound: an embankment cut through in the night, from the field side
a drowned meadow where the old channel came back
marks for the old course chiselled off
anchor: the mark cut where the old channel ran
a survey of both courses, old and new
a stretch of bank that has never been raised

features: water standing in a dry channel
a wet patch on a dry bank
a mark cut for the old course
an embankment cut from the field side
a drowned meadow
a straight cut in a winding river

decisions.cue: a dry channel with water standing in the bottom after weeks of no rain
decisions.cost: the river is coming back to it, slowly

resolve.success: you trace how far it has come back and can be somewhere else when it arrives
resolve.failure: you camp in the old channel and wake in it: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the channel alone; you take the long way round on the raised ground

decisions.cue: an embankment with a wet patch showing on the dry side
decisions.cost: the bank is going, from the inside

resolve.success: you find and stop the leak and the meadow behind stays dry, and they are grateful
resolve.failure: you dig at it to see and it goes while you are standing on it
resolve.orElse: leave it; the meadow floods behind you and the way back is under water

decisions.cue: a mark cut where the old channel ran, still legible
decisions.cost: the mark is the only proof the water was ever moved

resolve.success: you record the mark and can prove at the ending exactly what was done
resolve.failure: you chisel it out and there is no proof of anything, for anybody
resolve.orElse: leave it; somebody else takes it off before you come back

decisions.cue: an embankment cut through in the night from the field side
decisions.cost: somebody let the river out on purpose, onto somebody

resolve.success: you find whose field it was cut from and the transgression is laid bare
resolve.failure: you close the cut and the water goes where it was going before, onto others
resolve.orElse: leave the cut; the water keeps coming through and the ending is under it

decisions.cue: a straight cut where every other stretch of this water wanders
decisions.cost: the cut is engineering and the river hates it

resolve.success: you find the engineer's survey and know exactly what was promised and to whom
resolve.failure: you use the cut as a road and the water rises in it, quickly
resolve.orElse: go round by the ox-bow, costing a Turn in soft ground

decisions.cue: a drowned meadow where the old channel has come back
decisions.cost: the river has taken part of its course back already

resolve.success: you cross the meadow on the old causeway, which is still there under it
resolve.failure: you wade it and the old channel takes you as belonging to the field
resolve.orElse: go round the meadow entirely; it costs a Turn and the light

situations.doing: standing in a dry channel with water round its ankles that has no source
situations.onArrival: it points down the dry course and waits
situations.because: the water was moved and it stayed with the old line
situations.offer: walk the old course with it and the river treats you as belonging to it

situations.doing: pacing an embankment and writing nothing down
situations.onArrival: she asks whether you think the bank will hold
situations.because: she cut the new course and has been walking it ever since
situations.offer: tell her the truth and she will give you the survey of both channels

situations.doing: lying dry with water standing in the bottom of it
situations.onArrival: the standing water is moving very slightly, downstream
situations.because: the river was moved and is coming back a foot a year
situations.offer: walk it end to end and the water will not rise on you anywhere

situations.doing: standing in a drowned meadow up to the chest
situations.onArrival: they are facing the way the water used to run
situations.because: the meadow is the old course and it has come back
situations.offer: stand with them a moment and the meadow gives up what is under it

situations.doing: standing cut into a stone where the old channel ran
situations.onArrival: the cut is sharp and the stone around it is weathered soft
situations.because: it records where the water belongs and somebody kept it legible
situations.offer: read it aloud and the river will hear a claim made on its behalf

situations.doing: running in a straight cut where nothing else here runs straight
situations.onArrival: the water in the cut is flat and fast and does not sound like water
situations.because: it was straightened and never forgave it
situations.offer: offer to walk its old line and it will carry you where you ask

temptations.benefit: once, prove where something belongs
temptations.standingDrawback: the river expects you to put it back

temptations.benefit: know every channel here, old and new
temptations.standingDrawback: you know whose ground was sold to make it

temptations.benefit: once, hold a bank that is going
temptations.standingDrawback: the water goes somewhere else instead, onto somebody

temptations.cue: a sod off the never-raised bank
temptations.benefit: once, stand on ground the water respects
temptations.standingDrawback: the river treats the ground you left as forfeit

temptations.cue: a knowledge of the drowned causeway
temptations.benefit: cross flooded ground dry
temptations.standingDrawback: what is under the meadow uses it too

drowned.dangerLine: the river has one a year and it has not been given one in a long time

institution: a deep pool at the bend that has never been sounded
a stretch where everybody who goes in comes out at the same place
a village that has always known the number and never said it
ritual: something given to the water at the turn of the year, willingly
the drowned brought out at the same slack water and laid on the same stone
a wreath put on the pool each spring by somebody who lost one
demand: a pool lying dead flat in a wind
a laying-out stone, wet, with nothing on it
a wreath on the water that has not gone downstream
wound: a year when nobody was given and three were taken
the laying-out stone dry and cracked
wreaths from every year piled at the bank, none of them ever floated
anchor: what was given willingly, the one year
a list of every one it took, in order
a pool that gives them back

features: a pool flat in a wind
a wet laying-out stone with nothing on it
a wreath not going downstream
wreaths piled on a bank
a list of names in order
water going still around you

decisions.cue: a pool lying dead flat while there is wind on the trees
decisions.cost: the pool is attending to you specifically

resolve.success: you address it properly, out loud, and it will trade rather than take
resolve.failure: you throw something in to test it and it accepts that as the offering: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: go past on the far bank; it follows the bank you are on, all the way

decisions.cue: a laying-out stone, wet, with nothing on it
decisions.cost: the stone is kept wet by somebody, or by something being laid on it

resolve.success: you find who lays them out and they know every name the river has
resolve.failure: you lie down on it to look and the water comes up over the stone
resolve.orElse: leave it; you never learn what the count is or who is keeping it

decisions.cue: a wreath on the water that has not gone downstream
decisions.cost: the river is refusing it

resolve.success: you find out whose it is and why it was refused, and can put that right
resolve.failure: you push it off and it comes back and stays with you
resolve.orElse: leave it turning; the refusal stands and the ending has no way to be given

decisions.cue: wreaths from every year piled at the bank, none of them ever floated
decisions.cost: nobody has given willingly for a very long time

resolve.success: you count the years and know exactly how long the debt has been running
resolve.failure: you float them all at once and the river takes the arrears at once
resolve.orElse: leave the pile; the debt is unmeasured and the ending comes due anyway

decisions.cue: a list of every one it took, in order, cut into a post
decisions.cost: the last name is recent and the post is not finished

resolve.success: you read the list and can name the one it wants at the ending
resolve.failure: you cut a name of your own into it and the water accepts the entry
resolve.orElse: leave the post; you go to the ending with nothing to say

decisions.cue: water going still around your legs where you are standing in it
decisions.cost: it has chosen and it is being polite about the timing

resolve.success: you get out and give it something instead, immediately, and it accepts
resolve.failure: you stay in and it takes what it came for: -1 max Grit for the delve
resolve.orElse: refuse to enter the water at all; every crossing after this is contested

situations.doing: lying flat and dark in a wind that is moving everything else
situations.onArrival: it goes flatter when you come to the edge
situations.because: it takes one a year and has not been given one
situations.offer: offer it something of your own and it will let the reach alone

situations.doing: lying on a laying-out stone with its hands crossed
situations.onArrival: it turns its head to you without sitting up
situations.because: it went in willingly the year it was asked
situations.offer: tell it that it was thanked and it will name the one the river wants

situations.doing: piling wreaths on a bank that have never been floated
situations.onArrival: she asks whether you are here for this year's
situations.because: nobody will give and she keeps making them
situations.offer: float one with her and the pool will trade with you

situations.doing: turning on the water without going downstream
situations.onArrival: it holds against the current in front of you
situations.because: it was offered and refused
situations.offer: learn whose it is and the river will take an offering again

situations.doing: standing at the edge of the pool in the shape of somebody you almost know
situations.onArrival: the water is dead flat behind it and dead flat in front
situations.because: it has to take one and would much rather be given one
situations.offer: give it something you cannot afford and it will let everybody go

situations.doing: standing at the head of the pool with names cut into it in order
situations.onArrival: the last name is fresh and the wood below it is clean
situations.because: every one taken is cut in and the post is not finished
situations.offer: cut nothing, and read them all aloud, and the pool comes level

temptations.cue: what was given willingly, the one year
temptations.benefit: once, satisfy something that means to take somebody
temptations.standingDrawback: the river regards the account as reopened

temptations.benefit: once, be passed over by what takes one
temptations.standingDrawback: it takes the next nearest instead

temptations.benefit: know every name the river has
temptations.standingDrawback: you can see where the next line goes

temptations.cue: a chip off the laying-out stone
temptations.benefit: once, be brought out rather than kept
temptations.standingDrawback: somebody else is kept in your place

temptations.cue: a stretch of water gone still
temptations.benefit: once, cross without being taken
temptations.standingDrawback: the stillness follows you onto dry land
